newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sheep, lamb prices push NZ PPI up in Dec quarter.
newsitem.headline: Sheep, lamb prices push NZ PPI up in Dec quarter.

text.p: Output price levels of goods and services sold by New Zealand industries rose on average by 0.2 percent in the December quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
This follows a 0.4 percent increase in the September quarter.
Output price levels for the December quarter were 0.6 percent higher than those recorded a year earlier, compared to an annual increase to the September quarter of 0.4 percent.
SNZ said higher sheep and lamb livestock and meat prices contributed most to the increase, partially offset by lower wool, forestry product and basic metal prices.

The industry groups contributing the most to the outputs index rise were Agriculture (up 1.1 percent in the December quarter); Food, Beverages and Tobacco (up 0.8 percent); and Trade, Restaurants and Hotels (up 0.3 percent).
The Insurance and Financing industry outputs index fell 0.6 percent, due mainly to a fall in the financial service charge.

Input price levels of goods and services bought by New Zealand industries rose on average by 0.1 percent in the December quarter, excluding wages and depreciation. The annual rise to the December quarter, like that to the September quarter, was 0.4 percent.
SNZ said higher prices for crude oil and sheep and lamb livestock contributed the most to the rise in the inputs index, offset partially by lower prices for forestry products.

The industry groups contributing most to the rise were Trade, Restaurants and Hotels (up 0.7 percent in the December quarter); Construction (up 0.5 percent); and Agriculture (up 0.7 percent). A 1.3 percent fall in the Machinery and Metal Products index provided a partial offset to the increase.
